analysis.title: US: FOMC skipped but data shows higher rates required soon
key_insights: ANZ argued for a 25bp Fed rate increase at the October FOMC meeting. The Fed held rates unchanged, as widely expected.
ANZ does not read the hold as the end of the mini-tightening cycle. It now expects a 25bp increase at the December meeting and another 25bp increase in Q1 next year, probably in March.

Skipping a meeting departs from the sequential tightening seen early in hiking cycles over the past four decades. Chair Warsh explained the pause as a preference for more than one intermeeting set of data before changing rates. The move to seven live meetings in 2027 and six in 2028 reflects this preference.

Market-based core PCE disinflation earlier this year is reversing. It rose 0.34% m/m in September, up from 0.24% in August. The 3m annualised pace rose to 2.9% from 2.2% and the 6m annualised pace rose to 2.9% from 2.7%.

Preliminary Q3 GDP rose 3.4% saar after 2.2% in Q2. Real consumer spending rose 3.8% for a second consecutive quarter and real private investment rose 19.4% saar. ANZ says very strong growth increasingly risks fuelling demand-pull inflation.
The capex cycle is broadening beyond AI. Information processing equipment spending rose 37.4% (computers and peripherals +66.7%) and industrial equipment rose 24.7% after 27.0% in Q2.

Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, a measure of private domestic demand, rose 4.9%. Real federal consumption rose 15.8%, with non-defence consumption up 22.2%. Exports fell 5.7% and imports rose 19.7%.

ANZ says the FOMC cannot stay on hold much longer without repeating the 2021-22 policy error. Wage growth trends and a suspected rise in the economy's supply potential suggest inflation is less potent than then, but ANZ still wants the pickup in inflation and demand addressed quickly.

Warsh has called post-COVID inflation a major Fed policy error. ANZ says his tough Jackson Hole talk was not matched by an October hike, but further rate rises are inevitable. Only a sharp correction in financial markets may avoid them.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed funds target rate, October FOMC decision
macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held in October despite ANZ's case for a 25bp hike. ANZ does not treat the hold as the end of tightening.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed funds target rate, December meeting
macro_indicators.interpretation: ANZ expects the Fed to resume hiking in December, which supports a higher-for-longer rate path.
ANZ expects a second 25bp hike in Q1 next year, so two hikes in total across the next two hiking meetings.

macro_indicators.reading: 0.34% m/m in September, up from 0.24% in August
macro_indicators.interpretation: Monthly core inflation momentum is rising again, reversing the disinflation seen earlier this year.
The three-month pace has re-accelerated, which ANZ reads as re-intensifying inflation momentum.
The six-month pace is also rising, which confirms the trend beyond one month.
Growth accelerated, which ANZ says risks fuelling demand-pull inflation.

macro_indicators.reading: 3.8% saar for the second consecutive quarter

macro_indicators.interpretation: Investment is very strong and ANZ says the capex cycle is broadening beyond AI.

macro_indicators.indicator: Real final sales to private domestic purchasers
macro_indicators.interpretation: Private domestic demand is rising at the fastest pace since mid-2021, according to ANZ's Figure 2 title.

risk_factors: A repeat of the 2021-22 policy error if the Fed stays on hold while demand accelerates and inflation re-intensifies.
Demand-pull inflation from very strong growth, including a broadening capex cycle and a 15.8% rise in real federal consumption.
A sharp correction in financial markets is the only development ANZ names that could avoid further rate rises.

tension_points.bull_case: Wage growth trends and a suspected rise in the economy's supply potential suggest inflation is less potent than in 2021-22. Chair Warsh prefers more than one intermeeting set of data before changing rates, which argues for patience.
tension_points.bear_case: Market-based core PCE momentum is re-intensifying (3m annualised 2.9%) and demand is accelerating (Q3 GDP 3.4% saar, private domestic demand +4.9%). Staying on hold risks repeating the 2021-22 policy error.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp correction in financial markets, which ANZ says is the only thing that may avoid further rate rises.

theme_stances.key_argument: Re-intensifying core inflation momentum and very strong demand mean the Fed cannot stay on hold much longer.
